C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY.IntentSummary:
Author the execution for the approved, fingerprinted spec `.ngrace/changes/active/C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY/spec.xml` (ratified `approved`, gate permit and spec fingerprint `257f13dc…` recorded in the bundle's `run-ledger.xml`, commit `d84e37a`) and only within it; the plan conforms to the spec, it does not extend, narrow or reinterpret it. The spec fixes the payer-map deletion and its nine declarations, the two payment routes, the committed sequence, the write scope, the criterion mapping, and the faithful post-close copy — this plan takes all of that from the spec.
Three tasks carry the committed sequence. T-001 is the record work the spec's sequence step (1) names: the nine `<Pays>` declarations, the `F185` append, the born-live `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` historical row and the live `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` row, the shipped `--rewrite-roots`, the declared mid-state (`validator exit 1`, three findings), one `--retire` (`moved 3`), and the two suite repairs the moved state forces (the `bundleMinted` extension and the clamp-test deletion). T-002 is the spec's sequence step (2): delete `closedWithTokens`, `expandFTokens`, `expandFRange` and the `derivePayerMap` prose loop, remove the suite's one direct call site and the `Closed-with citation reduction` test, and land the prose-dead guard. T-003 is verification: the leaf suites, `bun run validate:ci`, the byte-invariance diffs, and the post-close reachability drive. The close is the authority's act and this plan's tasks end before it: no task writes `status="applied"`, no task renames the bundle into `.ngrace/changes/archive/`, no task runs the close's own `--retire` (which the spec declares reports `moved 2` — `F197` and the `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` row), and no task evaluates a `CloseEvidence`.
Why three tasks and not fewer or more. The fix budgets bind per task (`src/grace-cursor.ts:187` `FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET = 2`; `src/grace-cursor.ts:193` `FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4`, both re-read at this plan's commit `d84e37a13501fdbfaa8d0b0ed0201769ae1282a4`). T-001's failure-signature families are the record hand writes (escape shape, the two new rows' house form, the ten `<Pays>` appends), the root rewrite's read-back, the move's report, the walk authoring, and the suite repairs. Two honest fail→pass pairs are planned, one per write task, each far inside the budgets — signature-kind `test`, keys `cpi-carrier-row-walk-first` (T-001) and `cpi-prose-dead-guard-first` (T-002); the mid-state validator red below is the D28.1 enforcement, not a cycle, and is not counted. T-002's unplanned families are the engine deletion (residual references), the prose-dead guard, and the map byte-identity — three. Folding T-002 into T-001 would spend one task's budget on two independent write families (the record and the engine), which is the two-wave precedent's reason to split. Not a fourth task: the spec's Goal 3 lands the suite prose-path removals with the engine deletion, and separating them buys no budget window — the suite will not compile against a deleted export once the engine changes. T-003 is verification and the post-close drive, not a write task; its commands mutate only a throwaway copy.
The mid-bundle red is a declared working-tree state, never a commit. Inside T-001, after the four hand writes and `--rewrite-roots` (registry root `14 / 12 / 26`) and before the move, the shipped `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` exits 1 naming exactly three entries: `F185` (archive event `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`), `F198` (archive event `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`) and the born-live `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` row (archive event `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`). That is the D28.1 enforcement saying the move is due — a declared, verified working-tree state `validate:ci` can never see, because the same task's next act is the move and the commit holds only the moved state. One `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH` reports `moved 3`; the validator then exits 0. No task boundary and no recorded `Verification` command sits inside the red window. Which entries move when: mid-bundle, the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` row, `F185`, `F198`; at the close (the authority's), the `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` row and `F197`. Nothing else in the findings, rulings, registry or index genres moves.
The committed state machine, driven end to end on a whole-repository copy at this plan's commit (every exit code read directly; the copy is `/tmp/cpi-preclose` for the pre-close boundary and `/tmp/cpi-plan` for the post-close state, both left in place). Baseline `d84e37a`: findings `7673 / 173 / 7846`, rulings `1733 / 150 / 1883`, registry `12 / 14 / 26`, index `273 / 23 / 296`; the suite is 100 pass / 0 fail; the four record validators exit 0. T-001's boundary: registry `14 / 12 / 26` after the two live rows are born; `rewrite-roots ok`; validator exit 1 with the three named; `moved 3`; findings `7597 / 249 / 7846`, index `271 / 25 / 296`, registry `13 / 13 / 26`; validator exit 0; suite 101 pass / 0 fail (the clamp test deleted, the two walks added). T-002's boundary: the engine has zero `closedWithTokens` references, the suite 101 pass / 0 fail (the `:405` test deleted, the guard added), the derived map unchanged, `bun run validate:ci` exit 0. The close: `ngrace apply` archives the bundle, the close's `--retire` reports `moved 2`, findings `7569 / 266 / 7835`, index `270 / 26 / 296`, registry `12 / 14 / 26`, `F197` retired `<PaidBy>C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY</PaidBy>`, every `CloseEvidence` command and `bun run validate:ci` exit 0.
The suite repairs are exactly the two the spec forces, and no shipped assertion outside them is rewritten. (1) The `bundleMinted` extension in the `C-RECORD-PARSE payer derivation` test gains `F185: "C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY"`, `F198: "C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2"` and `F197: "C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY"`; the extension is consulted only for tokens the derivation actually mints, so the walk is green before the payments too. (2) The `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY clamp invariant` test (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:3068`) is deleted: it reduces to the two relations the shipped `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4` roots-invariant tripwire already asserts for all four roots, under a title that claims a clamp it does not assert, and its `headroom < 7 × median` clause is false after this bundle's moves (driven: mid-bundle headroom 249 against a product of 238; post-close 266 against 238). The deletion carries no criterion: the suite is green with the test present and absent, so a criterion asserting its absence would be un-failable (`F210`'s class); it is enforced by the spec's Goal 3(d), the spec's clamp Constraint, and T-001's acceptance criterion below. `F244` records the defect and its payment is a later flush's retired-row append to this bundle's row — not this bundle's `Pays`.
The mapping, fixed by the spec's own Constraint. Exactly one criterion — `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` — carries no `CloseEvidence` and must be mapped by exactly one task `Satisfies`; it is carried by T-003, this plan's only `Satisfies`. The other eleven criteria are close-bound and stay unmapped, because a `Satisfies` of a close-bound criterion is the shipped error `change.close-evidence-and-satisfied` (`src/lint/catalog.ts:286`), and an unmapped non-CloseEvidence criterion is the warning `AC-CLOSE-LINT`'s `--fail-on warnings` turns into an uncloseable bundle. Every `CloseEvidence` is evaluated only in the applied-archive state (`F196`'s rule), so T-003 writes its drive against the state the ceremony produces, never the pre-close tree.
`AC-PAYMENTS-LANDED`'s instrument, provided by this plan. The spec's criterion names "the production carrier and row walks in the suite (payment-invariant, walking both layers)"; measured at this plan's commit, no shipped walk covers `F185`, `F198`, `F197` or the two rows, and without one the criterion's `CloseEvidence` cannot fail for its claim — the `F210` class the spec removed elsewhere. An `AC-*`'s named instrument is part of the spec, and Goal 3's list is the forced repairs, not a ceiling on the suite; the suite is in the write scope. T-001 therefore adds the walks in the `C-FLUSH-AND-TEACH` house form: a carrier relation for `F185`, `F198`, `F197` — each, when a `<Finding>` carries it, exists at most once across the findings pair, its `status` agrees with the holding file, its index `<Entry>` layer agrees, and a retired carrier's `<PaidBy>` equals its payer (`C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`, `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`, `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY`), with the carrier-absent case green (payment-invariant: no token is pinned to a layer or a payment state) — and a row walk for `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` (`kind="historical"`, `<Pays>` exactly `F198`) and `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` (`kind="chartered"`, `<Pays>` exactly `F197`, `<StatusText>` house-form prose), each row exactly once across `registry.xml` and `registry-retired.xml` with its `status` agreeing with the holding file. The walk is written red-first and driven green at the T-001 and post-close states: 2 pass / 0 fail at each, including `F197` retired with `<PaidBy>C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY</PaidBy>` after the close's `moved 2`. Its red fixture mutates whichever layer holds the `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` row (F229's state-independent form) and is driven red on a mutated copy.
DurableScope is `<None />`, checked against the shipped predicate, not assumed: `isModuleOwnableWritePath` (`src/lint/core.ts:724`) returns false for every path outside `src/`, so none of the write-scope files is module-ownable and `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` cannot fire for the empty anchor set. The spec's `AffectedAreas` names no module; no second module list exists in this plan, and no synthetic module is minted.
The record's copy-drive obeys the flushed `F235`'s rule: a copy-drive of the record runs from inside a whole-repository copy, because the engine reads the archive from the process's cwd, and the plan-time faithful copy carries `.git` so the four `git diff --exit-code` criteria can run against the named base commit `af0f721`. Both driven at this plan's commit: T-001's boundary `--retire` reports `moved 0` and exits 0; the post-close drive reports `moved 2` and every criterion exits 0.
Every `file:line` below was re-read at this plan's commit before this plan was written (`F218`'s rule). Findings raised while this bundle is open go to `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` under the next staged number, never into the record under edit (`D30`); the buffer is read by this plan and written by no task.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The record writes, exact and byte-neutral where the spec says so. The nine declarations append the prose-minted tokens to the existing `<Pays>` cells of three `status="retired" kind="chartered"` rows in `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/registry-retired.xml`: `C-CRITERION-CLOSE-EVIDENCE` gains `[F100](#f100), [F101](#f101), [F102](#f102), [F103](#f103), [F104](#f104), [F105](#f105)`, `C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT` gains `[F112](#f112), [F113](#f113)`, and `C-SUPERSEDE-COMMAND` gains `[F125](#f125)`. The `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY` retired row's `<Pays>`, whose present bytes are `[F180](#f180), [F181](#f181).`, gains `[F185](#f185)`. These four edits change only the derived payment set: each token is carried by a retired finding (zero live carriers, measured), so no live finding's eligibility changes and the edit is byte-neutral for the map. The `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` historical row is born live in `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/registry.xml` with `<Pays>F198</Pays>` and the house form ("This row exists so the derivation can see the payment"), its `<Charter>` naming the rowless-archive survey and its `<StatusText>` a present-tree witness a reviewer can check without judgement: the `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` historical row in the retired sibling whose `<Pays>` is `F172`, `F172` retired with `<PaidBy>C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2</PaidBy>`, and `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`'s own measured population (55 archived bundles with no row in either layer). The `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` row is born live in `registry.xml`, `status="live" kind="chartered"`, `<Pays>` exactly `F197`, its `<Charter>` carrying the searched-before-minting statement with the measured counts (exact name zero archive directories and zero rows; `PAYMENT` 4 directories and 1 row; `INTEGRITY` 2 directories and 0 rows), and its `<StatusText>` house-form prose naming no `F`-token and carrying no "Closed with" sentence. Escape markup as character data (`<`, `>`, `&`) in every written cell; a cell whose witness text needs a tag writes it with entities, never paraphrased away. Then run the shipped writer `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --rewrite-roots` — never hand-edit a root; the registry root reads `base="14" headroom="12" ceiling="26"` after the two live rows (driven). Stop and report if a read-back exceeds a held ceiling; the remedy is never to raise it.

The declared mid-state and the one move, inside this task and never at a commit. After the writes and `--rewrite-roots` and before the move, the shipped `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` exits 1 naming exactly three entries — `F185` (archive event `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`), `F198` (archive event `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`) and the born-live `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` row (archive event `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`) — the D28.1 enforcement saying the move is due. This is a declared, verified working-tree state `validate:ci` can never see; no recorded `Verification` command runs inside it and no commit sits inside it. The same task then invokes exactly one `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH`, expected `moved 3`; a different count is a stop-and-report, never a number to adopt. The move retires the three entries: the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` row lands in `registry-retired.xml` with `status="retired"`; `F185` and `F198` land in `findings-retired.xml` with `status="retired"` and their `<PaidBy>` values, derived by the shipped writer from the map, `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY` and `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`; the three index `<Entry>` layers flip in place for `F185` and `F198`. The task reads the carriers back and reports them, and the walks added in the next criterion assert the landing durably. The roots after the move read findings `7597 / 249 / 7846`, index `271 / 25 / 296`, registry `13 / 13 / 26`, rulings `1733 / 150 / 1883`; the shipped validator then exits 0. Ceilings hold or fall and never rise.

The `AC-PAYMENTS-LANDED` walks, written red-first. In `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, add a production carrier relation and row walk in the `C-FLUSH-AND-TEACH` house form, in its own `describe`. (1) Carriers: for each of `F185`, `F198`, `F197`, when a `<Finding>` carries the token it exists at most once across `findings.xml` and `findings-retired.xml`, its `status` agrees with the holding file, its single index `<Entry>` carries the agreeing `layer`, and a retired carrier's `<PaidBy>` equals its payer (`C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`, `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`, `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY`); the carrier-absent case is green — the relation is payment-invariant and pins no token to a layer or a payment state. (2) Rows: `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2` (`kind="historical"`, `<Pays>` exactly `F198`) and `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` (`kind="chartered"`, `<Pays>` exactly `F197`, `<StatusText>` house-form prose) each exist exactly once across `registry.xml` and `registry-retired.xml` with the row's `status` agreeing with the holding file. The walk is written first, before any record write, and reds on the production record (the row walk reads zero rows — driven 0 pass / 2 fail, the fixture's `the mutated copy carries two C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY rows` precondition included); the writes, the move and the extension are the pass (driven 2 pass / 0 fail). Signature-kind `test`, key `cpi-carrier-row-walk-first`. Its red fixture mutates whichever layer holds the `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` row and verifies the mutation landed before reading the result (F229's state-independent form); driven red on a mutated copy. The relation is invariant under the close: `F197`'s retirement flips its carrier's status and index layer and the walk stays true (driven 2 pass / 0 fail post-close).

The two suite repairs this moved state forces, payment-invariant and F237/F238-safe. (1) Extend the `bundleMinted` map in the `C-RECORD-PARSE payer derivation` test with `F185: "C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY"`, `F198: "C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2"` and `F197: "C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY"`; the extension is the house form for a new payer and is consulted only for tokens the derivation actually mints, so the walk is green with the payments present and green before them. (2) Delete the `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY clamp invariant` test (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:3068`) in full — its `headroom < 7 × median` clause is false after this move (driven: 249 against 238) and its other two clauses are exactly what the shipped `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4` roots-invariant tripwire already asserts for all four roots, so it is a duplicate under a false title; the clamp behaviour stays with the synthetic `--retire` fixtures (`:524`, `:542`, `:567`, `:609`, `:661`, `:707`). No other shipped assertion is rewritten, and no assertion this or the next task adds pins a token to a layer or a payment state: every fixture that locates a holder walks both layers, and the two relations the deleted test duplicated stay carried by the tripwire. The suite at this task's boundary is 101 pass / 0 fail (100 shipped minus the deleted clamp test plus the two walks — driven). The working-tree red between the writes and the move is declared, not a planned failure cycle: this task's failure-signature families are the record hand writes, the root read-back, the move's report and the two suite edits — four distinct, inside the per-task distinct budget of 4 (`src/grace-cursor.ts:193`), with the same-signature repeat budget of 2 (`:187`).

The boundary and the close. T-002.Title: Delete closedWithTokens, expandFTokens, expandFRange and the derivePayerMap prose loop, and replace the deleted path's suite coverage with the prose-dead guard

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The engine deletion, complete and residual-free. In `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`, delete `closedWithTokens` (measured at this plan's commit `:338`), `expandFTokens` (`:359`), `expandFRange` (`:384`) and the second loop in `derivePayerMap` that calls `closedWithTokens` (`:424`); the private symbols go with the export, so no reference remains. `derivePayerMap` then mints from `<Pays>` only. The deletion never lands before T-001's declarations: alone it drops nine tokens from the derivation and reds the baseline; with the nine declared the map is byte-identical (driven: the production map's 93 tokens, every payer equal, plus `F185` and `F198`). `xmlDecode`, `whitespaceNormalize` and `F_TOKEN_RE` stay (each has another caller), and no import changes.

The suite's prose-path removal and its replacement red direction, exactly the spec's Goal 3(a). Remove the `closedWithTokens` import and its one direct call site — the `closedWithTokens(statusText)` assertion inside the `C-FLUSH-AND-UNPIN payment invariant` test at `:2503` — and delete the `Closed-with citation reduction` test at `:405`, whose expectation is the deleted path's behaviour (it drives the prose path through the validator on an isolated root and asserts `F100`–`F101` eligibility; it calls no function directly). Replace it with the prose-dead guard, which asserts the opposite on the same shape: over an isolated archive root (never the production record), a row named for an archive directory whose `<StatusText>` carries `Closed with F999 and F998.` and whose `<Pays>` is empty mints nothing; the same row with `<Pays>F999</Pays>` mints exactly `F999`. The guard is written first, against the un-deleted engine, and reds — the clean direction sees `F998` minted by the prose path (driven 0 pass / 1 fail); the engine deletion is the pass (driven 1 pass / 0 fail). Signature-kind `test`, key `cpi-prose-dead-guard-first`. The discriminating direction proves the instrument is not vacuously empty. The engine deletion and these suite removals land together (the suite will not compile against a deleted export). The `C-FLUSH-AND-UNPIN` payment-invariant test keeps its exactly-once, status and index-layer clauses and its isolated-root minting direction. Every assertion this task touches or adds locates its holder by walking both layers where a holder exists, pins no token to a layer or a payment state, and plants no fixture into the live layer.

The map identity and the mapping rules. After the deletion the derived map over the real archive and both registry layers is unchanged from T-001's state: no production token lost, no payer changed, `F185`/`F198` still minted by their rows (driven). The `C-RECORD-PARSE payer derivation` baseline test is green with the extended `bundleMinted`. This task's `Verification` commands and the plan's `TargetAssertions` contain no current-mode lint of this project root, checked by hand; each recorded command exits 0 at this task's boundary (driven: the suite is 101 pass / 0 fail, the three record validators exit 0, every byte-invariance diff exits 0). The executor emits its own execution-time cursor events and does not omit them; the close acts stay the authority's. Failure-signature families for this task: the engine deletion's residual references, the guard's authoring, and the map identity — three distinct, inside the per-task budget of 4, with the repeat budget of 2.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Task-observable suites, not manufactured reds. `bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`, `bun ./scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts`, `bun ./scripts/prove-record-preservation.ts` and `bun run validate:ci` all exit 0 at this task's boundary; the four `git diff --exit-code af0f721b5157f9598fb679736e33d8819cb0400a -- …` byte-invariance commands exit 0 (this task's boundary is the pre-close tree; the archive pathspec's own-arrival exclusion is harmless before the close and required after it). Do not manufacture a red for those commands being green at the prior task's state. This task carries the plan's single `Satisfies` (`AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE`); no task `Verification` command or `TargetAssertions` entry contains a current-mode lint of this project root, checked by hand (no `--assertions current`, and no `ngrace lint` of this root omitting `--assertions`). The post-close reachability drive, on a faithful whole-repository copy (`F235`), before recording pass — the rule `ngrace-plan` row 19 and the archived `C-FLUSH-AND-TEACH/plan.xml` T-005 fix, applied to this bundle. The verb archives the bundle and writes `applied` on both artifacts; then run `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH` from inside the copy: it reports `moved 2` (`F197` and the `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` row), the row sits in `registry-retired.xml` with `status="retired"`, `F197` sits in `findings-retired.xml` stamped `<PaidBy>C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY</PaidBy>`, its index layer is retired in place, and the roots re-derive (findings `7569 / 266 / 7835`, index `270 / 26 / 296`, registry `12 / 14 / 26`, rulings `1733 / 150 / 1883`); a second `--retire` reports `moved 0`. Then run **every** `CloseEvidence` `Command` the spec carries, from inside the copy, exit codes read directly: `bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (AC-PROSE-PATH-DEAD, AC-DECLARED-PAYMENTS, AC-PAYER-MAP-IDENTICAL, AC-PAYMENTS-LANDED, AC-RECORD-VALID, AC-ROOTS-HELD); the four `git diff --exit-code af0f721b5157f9598fb679736e33d8819cb0400a -- …` criteria exactly as the spec writes them (AC-NO-SRC, AC-RECORD-PRESERVED, AC-NO-ARCHIVE-EDIT, AC-DOCS-EXAMPLES), which is why the copy carries `.git`; and `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --fail-on warnings` (AC-CLOSE-LINT). A warning from `--fail-on warnings` is a finding for the report, never a reason to drop the command. Then run `bun run validate:ci` inside the copy, exit code read directly.
